searchText: **vbuterin** https://notes.ethereum.org/@vbuterin/r1v8VCULP **vbuterin** Curious if anyone has thoughts on this > **vbuterin** > Curious if anyone has thoughts on this <@!598575636012859412> the construction in approach 3 looks similar to "aggregate indexing" / feed aggregation, described on chapter 4.3 of "the book of swarm": https://swarm-gateways.net/bzz:/latest.bookofswarm.eth/ **vbuterin** hmm **vbuterin** kind of I guess, though imo it's serving a very different purpose **vbuterin** the purpose here is just as an intermediary system to prevent requiring each individual node to have 1000+ peers I would argue though that a standard laptop should be able to handle at least 500 connections just fine (if we drop from 16 to 8 peers per shard?) . Problems really appear if each connection incurs in too much overhead / processing / bandwidth, but for simple data sampling requests I'd expect to be fine. see https://drewww.github.io/socket.io-benchmarking/ and http://blog.mixu.net/2011/11/22/performance-benchmarking-socket-io-0-8-7-0-7-11-and-0-6-17-and-nodes-native-tcp/ with some interesting numbers for instance **vbuterin** hmm **vbuterin** 8 peers per shard feels uncomfortably low... **vbuterin** we need to assume the possibility of a fairly serious network attack ☝️ eclipse attacks are a very real threat and not particularly hard to execute in a peer to peer network. I worry about ETH1 already being quite susceptible just due to the relatively small number of validating clients connected to the network. agree, so maybe one does need a smarter connection topology .. Its hard to say though without doing some simulations/tests. Being against my own argument, it could also be that some ISPs will raise some red flags and block peers if they see 1k connections from a single customer.. **vbuterin** There are ways to make the design of a data availability focused network more robust. Particularly, if you see a chain that the network appears to be accepting as canonical, but you think it's missing data, you would try extra hard to look for intermediaries on those shards **sachayves** can you elaborate a little on why 16 may be enough, but 8 feels uncomfortably low (approach 1)? could 12 peers per shard (with intermediary nodes on ≈6 subnets each) work?
